title: 2 Samuel Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Samuel chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Samuel Chapter 15.

questions.question: What did Absalom prepare for himself after the events mentioned in 2 Samuel 15?
options: Chariots and horses with fifty men to run before him
A palace in Jerusalem
A large army of soldiers
A throne in Hebron
questions.correctAnswer: Chariots and horses with fifty men to run before him
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:1 states that Absalom prepared chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

questions.question: Where did Absalom stand early in the morning to meet people who came to the king for judgment?
options: Beside the way of the gate
On the rooftop of the palace
At the entrance of the temple
Near the brook Kidron
questions.correctAnswer: Beside the way of the gate
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:2 says Absalom rose early and stood beside the way of the gate to meet those coming for judgment.

questions.question: What question did Absalom ask those who came to him with controversies?
options: Of what city art thou?
What is thy complaint?
Who sent thee?
Why come you to the king?
questions.correctAnswer: Of what city art thou?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 shows Absalom asked, 'Of what city art thou?' to those who came to him.

questions.question: What reason did Absalom give for not hearing the people's matters himself?
options: There is no man deputed of the king to hear thee
He was too busy
He did not care for their issues
The king forbade him
questions.correctAnswer: There is no man deputed of the king to hear thee
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:3 says Absalom told them their matters were good but that no man deputed of the king was there to hear them.

questions.question: What did Absalom wish to be made in the land?
options: Judge
King
Priest
Captain of the army
questions.correctAnswer: Judge
questions.explanation: In 2 Samuel 15:4, Absalom said, 'Oh that I were made judge in the land.'

questions.question: How did Absalom greet the men who came to do him obeisance?
options: He put forth his hand, took them, and kissed them
He ignored them
He gave them gifts
He sent them to the king
questions.correctAnswer: He put forth his hand, took them, and kissed them
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:5 describes Absalom putting forth his hand, taking the men, and kissing them.

questions.question: True or False: Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel by his actions.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:6 states that by this manner Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

questions.question: After how many years did Absalom request to go and pay his vow to the LORD in Hebron?
options: Forty years
Ten years
Twenty years
Five years
questions.correctAnswer: Forty years
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:7 mentions 'after forty years' Absalom asked the king to let him go.

questions.question: True or False: Absalom vowed to serve the LORD if he was brought again to Jerusalem.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:8 records Absalom's vow that if the LORD brought him again to Jerusalem, he would serve the LORD.

questions.question: What was King David's response when Absalom asked to go to Hebron?
options: Go in peace
Stay in Jerusalem
Wait for my command
You shall not go
questions.correctAnswer: Go in peace
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:9 shows the king said, 'Go in peace' to Absalom.

questions.question: What did Absalom send throughout all the tribes of Israel?
options: Spies
Messengers of peace
Gifts
Soldiers
questions.correctAnswer: Spies
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:10 states that Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel.

questions.question: True or False: The two hundred men who went with Absalom from Jerusalem were aware of the conspiracy.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:11 says these men went in their simplicity and knew nothing of the plot.

questions.question: Who did Absalom send for from Giloh to join his conspiracy?
options: Ahithophel the Gilonite
Ittai the Gittite
Zadok the priest
Abiathar the priest
questions.correctAnswer: Ahithophel the Gilonite
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:12 states Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite from Giloh.

questions.question: What message did the messenger bring to David about the hearts of the men of Israel?
options: The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom
The men of Israel remain loyal to David
The people want peace
The tribes are divided
questions.correctAnswer: The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:13 reports a messenger told David that the hearts of the men of Israel were after Absalom.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 15, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Absalom sends spies throughout the tribes of Israel
David tells his servants to flee
Absalom prepares chariots and horses
David asks Zadok to carry back the ark of God
questions.correctAnswer: Absalom prepares chariots and horses
questions.explanation: According to 2 Samuel 15:1, Absalom’s preparation of chariots and horses is the first event among these options.

medium.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Samuel Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What reason did David give for fleeing Jerusalem when he heard the hearts of the men of Israel were with Absalom?
options: To avoid being captured and killed by Absalom
Because he wanted to punish the city
To prevent the city from being destroyed by the sword
Because he was afraid of his servants
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent the city from being destroyed by the sword
questions.explanation: David said to his servants to flee so that they would not be overtaken suddenly and bring evil upon the city, specifically to prevent it from being struck with the sword, as stated in 2 Samuel 15:14.

questions.question: How did the king's servants respond when David told them to flee from Absalom?
options: They hesitated and asked for more time
They fled immediately without question
They expressed readiness to do whatever the king appointed
They refused to leave the city
questions.correctAnswer: They expressed readiness to do whatever the king appointed
questions.explanation: The king's servants showed loyalty and readiness to obey David's command, saying they were ready to do whatever the king appointed, as recorded in 2 Samuel 15:15.

questions.question: What did David do with his concubines when he left Jerusalem?
options: He took them with him for protection
He left them to keep the house
He sent them to a neighboring city
He gave them to his servants for safekeeping
questions.correctAnswer: He left them to keep the house
questions.explanation: David left ten women, who were his concubines, to keep the house as he and all his household went out, as described in 2 Samuel 15:16.

questions.question: Which groups of soldiers accompanied David as he fled Jerusalem?
options: Only his household servants
Cherethites, Pelethites, and Gittites from Gath
The priests and Levites only
The men of Israel who remained loyal
questions.correctAnswer: Cherethites, Pelethites, and Gittites from Gath
questions.explanation: David was accompanied by all his servants and specifically the Cherethites, Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites who came after him from Gath, according to 2 Samuel 15:18.

questions.question: Why did David initially tell Ittai the Gittite to return to his place and not accompany him?
options: Because Ittai was a foreigner and exile
Because Ittai was too old to travel
Because David did not trust Ittai
Because Ittai had no men with him
questions.correctAnswer: Because Ittai was a foreigner and exile
questions.explanation: David told Ittai he was a stranger and exile and therefore should stay behind and not go up and down with them, as seen in 2 Samuel 15:19.

questions.question: How did Ittai respond to David's suggestion that he return to his place?
options: He agreed and returned immediately
He said he would serve David wherever he went, even unto death
He asked for more time to decide
He suggested David should flee alone
questions.correctAnswer: He said he would serve David wherever he went, even unto death
questions.explanation: Ittai declared his loyalty to David, promising to be with him whether in death or life, as found in 2 Samuel 15:21.

questions.question: What did David do with the ark of the covenant as he fled from Jerusalem?
options: He took it with him on the journey
He left it in the temple unguarded
He had Zadok and the Levites carry it but then told Zadok to return it to the city
He gave it to Absalom to keep
questions.correctAnswer: He had Zadok and the Levites carry it but then told Zadok to return it to the city
questions.explanation: Zadok and the Levites carried the ark out, but David instructed Zadok to carry it back into the city if he found favor with the LORD, as explained in 2 Samuel 15:24-25.

questions.question: According to David, what would be the sign that the LORD delights in him and will bring him back?
options: If he wins the battle against Absalom
If the people remain loyal to him
If he finds favor in the eyes of the LORD and sees the ark and His habitation again
If he captures Hebron
questions.correctAnswer: If he finds favor in the eyes of the LORD and sees the ark and His habitation again
questions.explanation: David said if he finds favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring him again and show him the ark and His habitation, as noted in 2 Samuel 15:25.

questions.question: What attitude did David express toward God's decision if He was displeased with him?
options: He would resist and fight back
He would accept whatever God deems good to do to him
He would try to make a new covenant
He would seek revenge against Absalom
questions.correctAnswer: He would accept whatever God deems good to do to him
questions.explanation: David said if God says He has no delight in him, then he will accept whatever God decides to do to him, as stated in 2 Samuel 15:26.

questions.question: What instruction did David give to Zadok and the priests regarding their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan?
options: To remain in the wilderness with David
To return to the city in peace and send information back to David
To join Absalom's army
To hide in the city until the conflict ends
questions.correctAnswer: To return to the city in peace and send information back to David
questions.explanation: David instructed Zadok to return to the city with his sons and to send news to him, as found in 2 Samuel 15:27 and 15:36.

questions.question: How did the people and David express their grief while leaving Jerusalem?
options: They sang songs of victory
They marched in silence
They wept with covered heads and barefoot as they went up Mount Olivet
They shouted curses against Absalom
questions.correctAnswer: They wept with covered heads and barefoot as they went up Mount Olivet
questions.explanation: David and all the people wept, covered their heads, and went barefoot as they ascended Mount Olivet, according to 2 Samuel 15:30.

questions.question: What was David's prayer regarding Ahithophel's counsel after it was revealed he joined Absalom's conspiracy?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David prayed that the counsel of Ahithophel would be turned into foolishness, as recorded in 2 Samuel 15:31.

questions.question: Did David want Hushai the Archite to accompany him or to return to the city to serve Absalom?
options: Accompany him to the wilderness
Return to the city and serve Absalom as a spy
Go to another land
Hide outside the city
questions.correctAnswer: Return to the city and serve Absalom as a spy
questions.explanation: David told Hushai to return to the city and pretend to serve Absalom in order to defeat Ahithophel's counsel, as explained in 2 Samuel 15:33-34.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue is demonstrated by David’s acceptance of God’s will as expressed in 2 Samuel 15:25-26?
options: Humility and trust in God's sovereignty
Revenge and retaliation
Pride and self-reliance
Fear and avoidance
questions.correctAnswer: Humility and trust in God's sovereignty
questions.explanation: David shows humility and trust by accepting God’s favorable or unfavorable decision regarding his fate, demonstrating faith and submission to God’s will (2 Samuel 15:25-26).

questions.question: What does 2 Samuel 15:27 promise will happen if the priests return to the city as David instructed in 2 Samuel 15:26?
options: They will become leaders of Absalom's court
They will secretly communicate news back to David
They will be captured by Absalom
They will abandon David
questions.correctAnswer: They will secretly communicate news back to David
questions.explanation: David instructs the priests to return to the city and send information to him through their sons, promising a communication link as a result of following his command (2 Samuel 15:26-27).

hard.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Samuel Chapter 15.

questions.question: Who did King David send back to Jerusalem with the ark of God while he tarried in the wilderness?
options: Zadok and Abiathar
Ahithophel and Hushai
Ittai and Jonathan
Ahimaaz and Jonathan
questions.correctAnswer: Zadok and Abiathar
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:29 states that Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there while David remained in the wilderness.

questions.question: What was David's emotional state as he ascended Mount Olivet, and how did he express it?
options: He wept, covered his head, and went barefoot
He rejoiced with music and dancing
He prayed silently with closed eyes
He fasted and wore sackcloth
questions.correctAnswer: He wept, covered his head, and went barefoot
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:30 describes David going up Mount Olivet weeping, with his head covered and barefoot, and the people accompanying him also covered their heads and wept.

questions.question: What was David's prayer regarding Ahithophel's counsel when he learned Ahithophel was among Absalom's conspirators?
options: That the counsel of Ahithophel be turned into foolishness
That Ahithophel be forgiven
That Ahithophel be removed from the conspiracy
That Ahithophel's counsel be accepted
questions.correctAnswer: That the counsel of Ahithophel be turned into foolishness
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:31 records David's prayer asking the LORD to turn Ahithophel's counsel into foolishness after hearing he joined Absalom's conspiracy.

questions.question: What role did Hushai the Archite agree to play in David’s plan against Absalom’s conspiracy?
options: Return to Jerusalem and pretend to serve Absalom to defeat Ahithophel's counsel
Stay with David and fight alongside him
Seek allies among the tribes of Israel
Go to Giloh to gather intelligence
questions.correctAnswer: Return to Jerusalem and pretend to serve Absalom to defeat Ahithophel's counsel
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:34 explains David's instructions to Hushai to return to Absalom as his servant to counter Ahithophel's advice and help David.

questions.question: Which two priests did David instruct Hushai to communicate with while in Jerusalem?
options: Zadok and Abiathar
Ahithophel and Zadok
Abiathar and Jonathan
Ahimaaz and Jonathan
questions.correctAnswer: Zadok and Abiathar
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:35 says David told Hushai to relay any information he hears in the king’s house to the priests Zadok and Abiathar.

questions.question: Who were the two sons of Zadok and Abiathar mentioned as part of the communication network for David?
options: Ahimaaz (Zadok’s son) and Jonathan (Abiathar’s son)
Ittai and Hushai
Ahithophel and Absalom
Jonathan and Ahithophel
questions.correctAnswer: Ahimaaz (Zadok’s son) and Jonathan (Abiathar’s son)
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:36 identifies Ahimaaz and Jonathan as the sons of Zadok and Abiathar, respectively, whom Hushai would use to send messages to David.

questions.question: What literary device is illustrated by the contrasting roles of Ahithophel and Hushai in this chapter?
options: Chiasm, showing reversal of counsel
Parallelism, repeating similar ideas
Metaphor, comparing counsel to weapons
Typology, foreshadowing Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm, showing reversal of counsel
questions.explanation: The chapter uses a chiasm by juxtaposing Ahithophel's wise counsel with Hushai’s counter-counsel to reverse Absalom’s rebellion plans (2 Samuel 15:31–36).

questions.question: In the cultural and historical context of ancient Israel, what was significant about David leaving ten concubines to keep the house?
options: It was a sign of his royal household's status and a political safeguard
It was a punishment for the concubines
It indicated David was planning to divorce them
It was a ritual cleansing before battle
questions.correctAnswer: It was a sign of his royal household's status and a political safeguard
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:16 shows David leaving concubines in the palace to maintain royal dignity and secure his household during his flight from Absalom.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'seer' in verse 27 suggest about Zadok's role?
options: He was a prophet or one who received divine revelation
He was a military commander
He was a royal scribe
He was a priest without prophetic function
questions.correctAnswer: He was a prophet or one who received divine revelation
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'seer' (ro'eh) in 2 Samuel 15:27 denotes one who receives visions or divine insight, highlighting Zadok's prophetic role in David's court.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of loyal support during adversity as shown by Ittai the Gittite's declaration in this chapter?
options: Ruth 1:16-17, Ruth’s loyalty to Naomi
Genesis 37:23, Joseph’s brothers plotting
Exodus 14:15, Crossing the Red Sea
Leviticus 19:18, Loving your neighbor
questions.correctAnswer: Ruth 1:16-17, Ruth’s loyalty to Naomi
questions.explanation: Ittai’s commitment to David (2 Samuel 15:21) parallels Ruth's vow of loyalty to Naomi (Ruth 1:16-17), both exemplifying devoted allegiance in hardship.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of trusting God's deliverance amid betrayal, as David prays to turn Ahithophel's counsel to foolishness?
options: Romans 8:28, God works for good
John 18:4-9, Jesus’ arrest and betrayal
Hebrews 11:32-34, Heroes of faith
Matthew 5:44, Love your enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 8:28, God works for good
questions.explanation: David's reliance on God's intervention despite betrayal (2 Samuel 15:31) echoes Romans 8:28, which assures believers that God works all things for good.

questions.question: What is the significance of David covering his head and going barefoot while weeping as he fled Jerusalem?
options: It was a sign of mourning and humility in ancient Israelite culture
It was a sign of royal celebration
It was a military tactic
It indicated ritual purity
questions.correctAnswer: It was a sign of mourning and humility in ancient Israelite culture
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:30 shows David’s actions as traditional signs of grief and humility, expressing sorrow over his son’s rebellion and his own vulnerable state.

questions.question: Which verse records David’s strategic use of communication through Zadok’s and Abiathar’s sons during the rebellion?
options: 2 Samuel 15:36
2 Samuel 15:28
2 Samuel 15:22
2 Samuel 15:16
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Samuel 15:36
questions.explanation: Verse 36 describes how Ahimaaz and Jonathan, sons of Zadok and Abiathar, respectively, would be used to send information to David during the crisis.

questions.question: True or False: David considered Ittai the Gittite as an outsider and sent him back to his own country for safety before fleeing Jerusalem.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Although David initially suggested Ittai return because he was a stranger (2 Samuel 15:19-20), Ittai declared his loyalty (verse 21), and David allowed him to continue with him (verse 22).

questions.question: True or False: Absalom’s conspiracy was strengthened by the increasing number of followers and the return of Ahithophel from Giloh.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 15:12 confirms that Ahithophel joined Absalom and the conspiracy gained strength as the people increased continually.

theological.title: 2 Samuel Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Samuel Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Absalom's act of positioning himself by the gate and receiving those with controversies reveal about his character in 2 Samuel 15:2-4?
options: His desire to administer justice as a king's representative
His manipulative ambition to gain favor and power
His genuine concern for the people's grievances
His role as a loyal servant to King David
questions.correctAnswer: His manipulative ambition to gain favor and power
questions.explanation: Verses 2-4 show Absalom calling people with disputes, telling them their matters are right but no one deputed by the king listens, then expressing a desire to be judge. This reveals a manipulative ambition rather than genuine justice, as he steals the hearts of the men of Israel (v6).

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by David leaving ten concubines to keep the house when he fled Jerusalem (2 Samuel 15:16)?
options: The doctrine of God's providential protection over the king's household
The doctrine of the priesthood of all believers
The doctrine of the sanctity of the royal lineage
The doctrine of separation from worldly things during trials
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's providential protection over the king's household
questions.explanation: By leaving concubines to keep the house (v16), David entrusts his household to God's providence, showing trust that God will protect what remains in Jerusalem while he flees, aligning with biblical teaching on divine providence (Psalm 121:3).

questions.question: How does David’s instruction to Ittai the Gittite in 2 Samuel 15:19-22 reflect the theme of loyalty and faithfulness in God’s people?
options: It shows that loyalty to the king is contingent on nationality
It emphasizes that faithfulness transcends cultural and national boundaries
It implies that only Israelites can serve God’s purposes
It highlights the rejection of foreigners in the covenant community
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes that faithfulness transcends cultural and national boundaries
questions.explanation: David tells Ittai, a foreigner and exile, that he may return to his place (v19-20), but Ittai pledges loyalty to David whether in death or life (v21). This shows faithfulness transcends ethnic origin, reflecting God’s inclusive covenant nature (Galatians 3:28).

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by David’s prayer concerning Ahithophel’s counsel in 2 Samuel 15:31?
options: God’s omniscience in foreseeing events
God’s justice in punishing sin
God’s sovereignty over human plans
God’s mercy in forgiving sinners
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty over human plans
questions.explanation: David prays that the counsel of Ahithophel would be turned into foolishness (v31), demonstrating his trust in God's sovereign power to override human conspiracies, consistent with Romans 8:28.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 2 Samuel 15:5-6 and 15:11 convey about human sin and deception?
options: That human hearts are easily deceived by outward appearances
That true justice is always evident to the people
That loyalty to God prevents deception
That political ambition is always righteous
questions.correctAnswer: That human hearts are easily deceived by outward appearances
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 show Absalom stealing hearts by flattering people with kisses, while 15:11 shows men going with Absalom in simplicity, unaware of the conspiracy. Together, these reveal mankind's susceptibility to deception by outward charm and falsehood (Jeremiah 17:9).

questions.question: How does the narrative of David’s flight in 2 Samuel 15:23-30 foreshadow Christ’s own suffering and rejection?
options: Both experienced rejection and wept silently in the wilderness
Both were crowned kings in their time of suffering
Both immediately defeated their enemies by power
Both fled to Gentile territories for refuge
questions.correctAnswer: Both experienced rejection and wept silently in the wilderness
questions.explanation: David wept with covered head and barefoot (v30), symbolizing mourning and humiliation, paralleling Christ’s suffering and rejection in the wilderness (Matthew 4:1-11; Luke 19:41). This typology shows David as a messianic figure.

questions.question: What theological principle is taught by David’s instruction to Zadok and Abiathar to return to Jerusalem with the ark in 2 Samuel 15:25-29?
options: The principle of trusting God’s presence and judgment amid trials
The principle that the ark must always accompany the king
The principle that God’s presence depends on human loyalty
The principle that the temple is less important than the king
questions.correctAnswer: The principle of trusting God’s presence and judgment amid trials
questions.explanation: David sends the priests back with the ark, stating if he finds favor with the LORD, He will bring him back (v25). This shows trust that God’s presence and judgment are sovereign and not dependent on David’s physical presence, reflecting faith in divine providence.

questions.question: What does Absalom’s use of trumpets and spies as described in 2 Samuel 15:10-12 reveal about the nature of his rebellion?
options: It was a strategically planned political coup
It was a spontaneous and unorganized uprising
It was a peaceful petition for justice
It was an act approved by King David
questions.correctAnswer: It was a strategically planned political coup
questions.explanation: Absalom sends spies throughout Israel and instructs them to proclaim his reign at the trumpet sound (v10), and secures Ahithophel’s counsel (v12). These actions show calculated political strategy, not a mere protest or petition.

questions.question: How does the chapter 2 Samuel 15 demonstrate the human sin of pride through Absalom’s actions?
options: By his desire to replace David and make himself judge
By his obedience to his father’s will
By his humility before the elders of Israel
By his withdrawal from political life
questions.correctAnswer: By his desire to replace David and make himself judge
questions.explanation: Absalom’s ambition to be judge and king (v4, 10) reveals pride and desire for power, highlighting human sinfulness in seeking authority apart from God’s appointment (Proverbs 16:18).

questions.question: What combined theological theme is found in 2 Samuel 15:13-14 and 15:31 concerning God’s control over political upheaval?
options: God remains sovereign even when human hearts turn rebellious
Political power is independent from divine authority
God condones rebellion against kings
Human plans are always successful without God
questions.correctAnswer: God remains sovereign even when human hearts turn rebellious
questions.explanation: Though the hearts of Israel turn to Absalom (v13-14), David prays to frustrate Ahithophel’s counsel (v31), showing God’s sovereignty over rebellion and political conspiracies (Psalm 2:1-4).

questions.question: What apologetic response does 2 Samuel 15:25-26 provide to sceptics who claim that God's favor is unpredictable and arbitrary?
options: The text shows David’s submission to God’s will, indicating God’s favor is relational and based on covenant faithfulness
It proves God arbitrarily favors some and rejects others without reason
It illustrates that human effort alone secures God’s favor
It denies any connection between human actions and God’s favor
questions.correctAnswer: The text shows David’s submission to God’s will, indicating God’s favor is relational and based on covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: David says if God delights in him, He will restore him; if not, let God do as He pleases (v25-26). This expresses submission to God’s just and relational favor grounded in covenant, not randomness, consistent with Deuteronomy 7:9.

questions.question: What do David’s weeping and covered head in 2 Samuel 15:30 signify regarding sanctification and spiritual mourning?
options: They demonstrate godly sorrow and humility in the face of sin and loss
They indicate physical weakness and despair without faith
They represent rejection of God’s will
They exemplify shame for personal sin only
questions.correctAnswer: They demonstrate godly sorrow and humility in the face of sin and loss
questions.explanation: David’s weeping and covered head signal mourning and humility (v30), reflecting sanctification as godly sorrow producing repentance (2 Corinthians 7:10), acknowledging the consequences of sin and betrayal.

questions.question: In 2 Samuel 15:32-37, what theological principle is illustrated by David sending Hushai back to Absalom with a counter-counsel mission?
options: The principle of divine wisdom working through human agents to protect the righteous
The rejection of all political intrigue by God
The reliance on military might over spiritual counsel
The futility of trusting friends in times of crisis
questions.correctAnswer: The principle of divine wisdom working through human agents to protect the righteous
questions.explanation: David sends Hushai to counter Ahithophel’s counsel (v34), using human wisdom aligned with divine providence to frustrate evil plans, showing God’s protective guidance (Proverbs 21:30).

questions.question: How does 2 Samuel 15 illustrate the biblical doctrine of human free will and divine sovereignty working together?
options: Absalom freely conspires, but God sovereignly controls the outcome
David’s flight shows human weakness overriding divine plans
God forces Absalom to rebel without choice
Human free will is denied by all events in the chapter
questions.correctAnswer: Absalom freely conspires, but God sovereignly controls the outcome
questions.explanation: Absalom plans rebellion (vv10-14), exercising free will, yet David prays for God to frustrate Ahithophel’s counsel (v31), showing divine sovereignty ultimately governs human actions (Isaiah 46:10).

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does 2 Samuel 15 make with the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: It anticipates the suffering servant motif fulfilled in Christ
It concludes the history of Israel’s monarchy
It focuses solely on political intrigue without spiritual meaning
It rejects the idea of a Messiah completely
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the suffering servant motif fulfilled in Christ
questions.explanation: David’s humiliation and flight (v30) foreshadow Christ’s passion as the suffering servant (Isaiah 53), linking Old Testament kingship with messianic fulfillment.
